candidates.name: waybackpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library + CLI wrapping the Internet Archive Wayback Machine SavePageNow, CDX Server, and Availability APIs. No committed data; pip-installable, ~500 commits, MIT licensed, actively maintained with Docker image. Would let us pull CDX listings of every archived snapshot of a given airbnb.com, airdna.co, or mashvisor.com URL and fetch specific dated captures.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers gap #17 (Wayback Machine tooling). Could be pointed at historical insideairbnb.com pages (their CDN only keeps ~1yr per our notes) or at archived AirDNA/Mashvisor market-stat pages to recover realised-occupancy/ADR claims from past years (gap #2) that are otherwise gone.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified in README but actively maintained (CI badges, recent release notes)
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as Wayback Machine's index for the target URL

candidates.name: waybackpack
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI (pure Python, requests only) that downloads every archived snapshot the Wayback Machine holds for a given URL, or just lists snapshot URLs, filterable by date range. 3.2k stars, 114 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Bulk-download tool for reconstructing a time series of archived pages (e.g. an Inside Airbnb city page, an AirDNA market-stats page, or an Airbnb press/newsroom page) rather than one snapshot at a time; complements waybackpy for gaps #1/#2/#17.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, but 3.2k stars indicate long-standing/actively used
candidates.time_coverage: full Wayback Machine index depth for target URL

candidates.name: wayback-machine-downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby gem (5.9k stars, 293 commits, MIT) that downloads an entire archived website (all pages, all timestamps or a filtered range) from the Wayback Machine, rebuilding the original directory/URL structure rather than IA's rewritten links.
candidates.why_useful: Could mirror an entire historical insideairbnb.com or a competitor's market-data microsite (AirDNA blog/market reports, Mashvisor city pages) as it existed at past dates, filling the pre-2023 Inside Airbnb gap (#1) or reconstructing STR occupancy claims (#2).
candidates.last_activity: unspecified; 808 forks, 127 watchers, actively used tool

candidates.name: wayback-machine-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapy-based crawler/CLI (482 stars, 42 commits, ISC license) that crawls and saves archived snapshots of a whole site over a specified date range, with regex allow/deny rules for which URL paths to follow.
candidates.why_useful: More configurable than wayback-machine-downloader for a targeted crawl (e.g. only AirDNA's 'market data' subpages, or Inside Airbnb's per-city summary pages) across many dates at once — useful for gaps #1 and #2.
candidates.time_coverage: full Wayback Machine depth, configurable range

candidates.name: wayback (EDGI)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client library (977 commits, BSD-3-Clause) from the Environmental Data & Governance Initiative for finding/loading historical Wayback Machine captures of specific URLs; built for their environmental-page monitoring work but generic.
candidates.why_useful: Well-maintained alternative to waybackpy with a more research-oriented API (used in academic replication pipelines); same use case for gaps #1, #2, #17.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, actively developed by an established org (EDGI)

candidates.name: cdx_toolkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit (211 stars, 287 commits, Apache-2.0) that unifies querying Common Crawl's monthly CDX indices and the Internet Archive Wayback CDX API behind one interface (`--cc` / `--ia` flags), and can extract matched captures into WARC files.
candidates.why_useful: We already hold a Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows); this tool would let us extend the same CDX-query workflow to the Wayback Machine's own (larger, longer-history) CDX index for airbnb.com, AirDNA, Mashvisor or insideairbnb.com without hand-rolling API calls, and pull matching WARC pages for gaps #1/#2.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, beta but actively maintained per README
candidates.time_coverage: Common Crawl (2008-present) + full Wayback CDX depth
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends our existing Common Crawl CDX holding to the Wayback Machine index

candidates.name: cdx-summary (cdxsummary)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool (pip: cdxsummary; 100 stars, 125 commits, AGPL-3.0) that summarizes a CDX file (local, remote, gz/bz2, or a live Wayback CDX Server query / Petabox item): capture counts, unique URLs/hosts, MIME/status distributions, year/month breakdowns, top hosts, sample memento URLs.
candidates.why_useful: Quick reconnaissance layer before a full crawl — could scope how many archived captures exist for airbnb.com press/newsroom paths, insideairbnb.com, or airdna.co/mashvisor.com by year before committing to a full waybackpack/downloader pull.
candidates.time_coverage: matches whatever CDX index is queried

candidates.name: gau (getallurls)
candidates.what_it_holds: Go CLI (MIT, 171 commits) that fetches every known historical URL for a domain by combining AlienVault OTX, the Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, and URLScan, with filters by extension/status/MIME.
candidates.why_useful: URL-discovery step to enumerate what paths ever existed under airdna.co, mashvisor.com, or insideairbnb.com (e.g. old market-report slugs, city pages that later moved/disappeared) before running a downloader against the Wayback Machine — feeds gaps #1/#2.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, actively maintained (23 open issues, 12 PRs)
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as each underlying index goes

candidates.name: waybackurls
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Go tool (4.6k stars) that lists every URL the Wayback Machine has archived for a given domain (pipe domains in, get URLs out).
candidates.why_useful: Simpler single-purpose alternative to gau for the same URL-discovery use case against AirDNA/Mashvisor/Inside Airbnb domains.
candidates.license: unspecified in fetched content (commonly MIT upstream)
candidates.time_coverage: full Wayback CDX depth for the domain

candidates.name: ArchiveSpark
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache Spark framework (Internet Archive-authored, MIT, 162 stars, 154 commits) for large-scale filtering/extraction/derivation over web-archive collections (WARC/CDX), including direct access to Wayback Machine holdings; outputs to JSON while preserving data lineage.
candidates.why_useful: If a large-scale pull of archived Airbnb/AirDNA/Inside-Airbnb pages across many years and thousands of URLs is ever attempted, this is the scale-appropriate processing layer (vs. one-off scripts) — same use case as our existing Common Crawl WARC renders (3,000 already pulled) but for Wayback's index.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, versioned to 3.0 with recent namespace updates
candidates.time_coverage: matches whatever archive collection is targeted

candidates.name: ipwb (InterPlanetary Wayback)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed project (1,622 commits) that converts WARC files to IPFS-distributed archives and replays them; includes only small sample WARC files for testing, no real datasets.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal for our purposes — a decentralized-storage/replay layer, not an acquisition method for new data. Flagged for completeness under 'Wayback tooling' but not directly actionable.

candidates.name: archivenow
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed tool (434 stars, 186 commits) to push a live URL into multiple public archives at once (Internet Archive, Archive.today, Perma.cc, Megalodon.jp) via CLI, Python library, web service, or Docker; can also produce local WARC files.
candidates.why_useful: Forward-looking companion to the retrieval tools above: could be used going forward to proactively archive AirDNA/Mashvisor market pages or Airbnb newsroom/investor pages on a schedule so future point-in-time snapshots exist (addresses the point-in-time rule in our own CLAUDE.md, not retroactive data).
candidates.last_activity: last noted feature change January 2021 (removed WebCite/Archive.st)
candidates.time_coverage: prospective only (captures made from now on)

candidates.name: MemGator
candidates.what_it_holds: Go-based Memento aggregator (2.2k-star family topic listing shows it at 80 stars under a related search) that queries multiple web archives at once (Internet Archive, archive.today, UK Web Archive, etc.) via the Memento protocol (RFC 7089) to find all known archived copies of a URL.
candidates.why_useful: Cross-archive discovery (not just the Internet Archive) for old AirDNA/Mashvisor/Inside-Airbnb pages that might have been captured only by a national web archive rather than archive.org.

candidates.name: awesome-memento
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list (122 stars) of Memento-protocol / web-archiving software and literature: py-memento-client, mcurl, memento-cli, MemGator, and academic papers on temporal web archiving.
candidates.why_useful: One-stop index to find additional Wayback/Memento clients beyond what a keyword search surfaces directly; useful as a jumping-off point for a deeper follow-up pass on this theme, not itself a data source.

candidates.name: ArchiveBox
candidates.what_it_holds: Large (28.4k stars) self-hosted web-archiving tool that takes a list of URLs/browser history/bookmarks and saves full-fidelity local copies (HTML, JS, PDFs, media, screenshots, WARC) going forward; not a Wayback Machine retrieval tool per se but a self-hosted archive-creation tool that can also import existing Wayback snapshots.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at a watch-list of AirDNA/Mashvisor/Airbnb newsroom URLs to start building our OWN point-in-time archive from today forward (complements the retroactive Wayback-retrieval tools above); large, actively maintained, well-documented.
candidates.size_hint: self-hosted tool, storage scales with what you archive

notes: This theme turned out to be almost entirely METHOD-only: extensive searching (both WebSearch, until the shared session budget was exhausted after 4 queries, and WebFetch against github.com/search, Bing, DuckDuckGo html/lite, and Mojeek, most of which were rate-limited or CAPTCHA-blocked) found no GitHub repository that already holds a committed dataset of archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA/Mashvisor market pages, or an archived mirror of the Inside Airbnb site. What exists is a mature ecosystem of generic Wayback Machine / Memento / CDX client libraries and crawlers (waybackpy, waybackpack, wayback-machine-downloader, wayback-machine-scraper, cdx_toolkit, gau, waybackurls, ArchiveSpark, MemGator, etc.) — well-documented, MIT/BSD/Apache licensed, all client-side tools that would need to actually be RUN against airbnb.com/airdna.co/mashvisor.com/insideairbnb.com to produce anything, which per the run rules ('do not run scrapers... a human decides terms-of-service questions') is out of scope for this cataloguing pass. I did not find a single repo combining Wayback tooling with a pre-built Airbnb/STR dataset, so I rated everything low-to-medium and flagged the two most functionally distinct/mature options (waybackpy for single-URL work, wayback-machine-downloader or wayback-machine-scraper for whole-site historical crawls, cdx_toolkit to unify with our existing Common Crawl CDX workflow) as the medium-potential picks. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: github.com/search itself returned HTTP 429 (Retry-After 3600) on every attempt after the first few calls — likely because other scouts running in parallel are consuming the same rate limit window — so a proper github.com native search for combinations like 'airbnb wayback', 'AirDNA archive', 'insideairbnb wayback', 'mashvisor scrape' could not be completed; github.com/topics/* pages worked and were used instead, but topic pages only surface the most-starred repos per topic and will miss small/niche repos (e.g., a student project archiving AirDNA market pages with <20 stars would not appear). A follow-up scout with either a fresh WebSearch budget or working `gh search` access should re-run targeted queries: 'insideairbnb wayback', 'airdna archive scrape', 'mashvisor historical', 'airbnb.com archived snapshot dataset', and check Kaggle/Zenodo for any 'archived Airbnb pages' dataset that a GitHub README merely points to.
